best_for: Students and teachers starting with Python who want one installer that runs code and shows what each line does, without setting up an interpreter first.

points.title: Python comes in the box
points.text: The installer bundles Python 3.14, so beginners can write and run code right away. You can point Thonny at a separate Python install later.

points.title: Watch code run step by step
points.text: Ctrl+F5 steps through a program without setting breakpoints, F6 takes big steps and F7 small ones. The Variables view shows values change as you go, which makes bugs easier to explain in class.

points.title: Packages without the command line
points.text: Tools, Manage packages gives a simple screen over pip for installing third-party libraries.

points.title: Built for learning, not big projects
points.text: Thonny starts with a plain interface on purpose and hides features that distract new learners. Experienced developers working on large codebases will likely want a full editor instead.

points.title: Free on every desktop
points.text: Thonny is MIT licensed. Windows installers come for x64 and Arm64, per user or for all users, with a portable zip as well. Macs get Intel and Apple Silicon packages.

points.title: Flatpak is from the author
points.text: The Flathub build for x64 and Arm64 is verified as published by Aivar Annamaa. The Windows listing keeps 35 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.
